Oregon FIA calibration data: the trees behind the mortality counts

Source: R/data.R
fia_tree_dt.Rd

One row per tree and remeasurement interval for the fia_obs_dt training sites (fia_tree_dt) and the fia_obs_test holdout sites (fia_tree_test): every tree alive at the start of an interval, with its diameter then and its fate over the interval. These are the closed cohorts whose counts (n_at_risk, n_died) the site tables carry, and the tree_data of fit(loss_aggregation = c(mortality = "tree")) and predictTrees(), which score the mortality function on every observed tree instead of on the site's pooled rate (see finn_loss). The ids, time axis and species coding are those of the site tables, so the two join on siteID, year and species. All trees of the FIA macroplot are kept: the per-tree loss scores fates and needs no area expansion.

Usage

fia_tree_dt

fia_tree_test

Format

A data.table with one row per tree and interval (9979 rows and 661 deaths / 10109 rows and 734 deaths) and 8 columns:

siteID, year

site index and the census that closes the interval, on the axis of fia_obs_dt (10, 20; 21 or 22).

patchID

patch (FIA subplot) index, as in fia_init_trees.

species

species index 1..11 (fia_species_dt), the species the tree was recorded as at the start of the interval.

dbh

diameter at breast height at the start of the interval, cm.

growth

the tree's yearly relative growth rate over the interval, (dbh_end / dbh)^(1 / period_length) - 1; NA for a tree that died.

died

1 if the tree was dead at the end of the interval, 0 if alive.

period_length

years from the start to the end of the interval, as in fia_obs_dt.

An object of class data.table (inherits from data.frame) with 10109 rows and 8 columns.

Source

A seeded subsample of Oregon plots of the US Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) database, with WorldClim bioclimatic variables attached per plot. The preparation script and the provenance of the source tables are in the package repository (dev/make_extdata.R, data-raw/README.md).

Details

In a few cells (21 of the training and 22 of the holdout site x year x species cells) the tree table holds trees that the site table's counts do not: the site table has no row for a species whose trees had all died by a census. The tree table keeps them (5 and 7 deaths); everywhere else the counts agree exactly. Two holdout sites whose first inventory found only dead trees have no tree at risk and so no row.

See also

fia_obs_dt, predictTrees(), finn_loss

Other fia datasets: fia_env_dt, fia_init_trees, fia_obs_dt, fia_species_dt

Examples

library(data.table)
# deaths and trees at risk per interval, and the yearly mortality by size class
fia_tree_dt[, .(trees = .N, deaths = sum(died)), by = year]
#>     year trees deaths
#>    <int> <int>  <num>
#> 1:    10  4935    279
#> 2:    20  5044    382
fia_tree_dt[, .(trees = .N, annual_mortality = round(1 - (1 - mean(died))^(1 / 10), 4)),
            by = .(dbh_class = cut(dbh, c(0, 20, 30, 45, 61, 80, 100, Inf)))][order(dbh_class)]
#>    dbh_class trees annual_mortality
#>       <fctr> <int>            <num>
#> 1:    (0,20]  3010           0.0084
#> 2:   (20,30]  2502           0.0087
#> 3:   (30,45]  1624           0.0058
#> 4:   (45,61]   734           0.0047
#> 5:   (61,80]   982           0.0049
#> 6:  (80,100]   702           0.0030
#> 7: (100,Inf]   425           0.0033
